page.layout: Running head at top centre; page number top right. Two medallion engravings (Leo Armenius left, Michael Balbus right) above the text. Below them one column of running text in two paragraphs.

main_text.p: LEO Armenius, huius nominis Constantinopolis Imperator quintus, ac post Carolum magnum Romanorum Imperatorem, quartus à Nicephoro, dum in oriente Michaëlis supradicti Imperatoris Duce agit, ad imperium aspirans seditione in exercitu excitat, factúsque est à militibus Imperator ann. mun. 4775. à Christo nato 813. hic vbi regiâ ingressus est, Michaëlis filium abscissis genitalibus in exilium misit. victoriam de Bulgaris retulit, Thraciâ recuperauit, quàm plurimos hostes cepit, repressitque eorum audaces conatus, qui iam Adrianopoli potiti, in Constantinopolim arma meditabatur. Diuorum imagines quas fustulerat ipse, cum nollet restituere, noctu per insidias dū sacris operatur, in ipso templo ab imaginum cultoribus capite truncatur, ac multis confoditur vulneribus, anno imperij octauo: vxor in monasterium truditur, filij in exilium pelluntur. Vide Egn. lib.2. ac Cosmographiam Munsteri lib.4. & Blond.

MICHAEL Balbus prauissimis moribus imbutus, qúeque Leonē prædictum confoderat, imperat Constantinopoli anno mundi 4783. à Christo nato 821. Hic humili ac sordido loco natus, Thomam virum quidem obscurum, qui tyrannidē inuaserat, vario primùm rerum euentu aggressus, tandem oppressit: cùm prius eò desperationis deductus esset, vt ex arce Constantini ad Peram, oppidulum, ferreā catenā produxisset. Itaque traditum sibi Thomā, qui Adrianopolim se receperat, manibus pedibúsq; truncauit, multisque cruciatibus affectum, tandè iugulauit. Saraceni hoc principe Cretam occupant, totámq; ferè in ditionē redigunt, Græcos duplici vincunt prælio. Obiit Michaël vētris profluuio anno imperij nono. Vetus oraculum innotuit, tum rem Romanam ruitura, cùm & Balbus & auarissimus princeps imperaret. Vide vt supra.

page.notes: Two medallion engravings above the text carry legends: left "LEO ARMENIVS" (partly cut off at the left edge, "...NIVS" and "LEO ARM..."), right "MICHAEL BALBVS" (partly cut off, "BALBVS" and "MICHAEL"). These are part of the illustrations and are not transcribed as text. Printed "ann .mun." has a stray space, left as printed. The "dū" in "per insidias dū sacris" is uncertain (the mark over the u may be a macron or a tilde), so it could be "dū" or "dum": [?] not added because the reading is clear enough in context.
